summary: Moderate difficulty: the authorization code flow works on development stores right away, but public distribution requires Shopify app review before merchants outside your own stores can install. Shopify app review, which also covers App Store registration with a one-time fee, is the main thing that can hold up launch.
cost: One-time Shopify App Store registration fee (amount not stated in the pages)
appType: Public-distribution standalone app using the authorization code grant, because the agent's backend runs outside the Shopify admin and many merchants install it.
handoff: An agent can choose the scopes and build each store's authorize link; you create the app, release a version, copy the credentials, connect a development store, choose the distribution, request protected customer data access and submit for review.

gates.title: Public distribution needs the App Store registration
gates.what: Public distribution requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee. The distribution method cannot be changed after selection.
gates.where: Dev Dashboard → app Home → Distribution card → Select distribution method
gates.todo: Register for the App Store, pick Public distribution on the production app, and confirm the fee.

gates.title: Customer data is only fully available on development stores before approval
gates.what: Without approval, protected customer data fields are not returned on non-development stores. Test on development stores before launch.
gates.where: Partner Dashboard → Apps → your app → API access requests
gates.todo: Test on a development store and select the data fields you use in the Partner Dashboard.

gates.title: Shopify must review public apps
gates.what: Public distribution requires approval. Protected customer data (levels 1 and 2) also requires review for public apps.
gates.where: Partner Dashboard → Shopify App Store review page
gates.todo: Fix issues flagged on the review page, then click Submit your app.

gates.title: No organization admin approval step is documented
No paid API tier is documented
Ongoing obligations are unclear
gates.what: Apps using level 2 protected customer data must participate in data protection reviews.
gates.todo: Be ready to provide evidence of your data practices if contacted.

requirements.text: A Shopify account with app development permissions in the Dev Dashboard.
A development store to install and test the app.
Budget for the one-time Shopify App Store registration fee.

steps.text: Decide which scopes the app needs: a read_* or write_* scope per resource (write includes read).
steps.detail: read_orders covers only the last 60 days; add read_all_orders for older orders.

steps.text: Dev Dashboard → Apps: click Create app, choose Start from Dev Dashboard, name the app and click Create.
Dev Dashboard → your app → Versions: set the App URL and scopes, then click Release.
steps.detail: An app that isn't embedded in the Shopify admin can keep the default App URL. A store can't install the app until it has a released version.

steps.text: Dev Dashboard → app settings: add your callback URL as a redirect URI.
steps.detail: It must exactly match the redirect_uri you send in the authorize request.

steps.text: Dev Dashboard → your app → App settings: copy the Client ID and Client secret into your backend configuration.
Build the authorize link for the merchant's store from your client ID, scopes, redirect URI and a random state.
steps.detail: Each store has its own link: https://{shop}/admin/oauth/authorize?client_id=…&scope=…&redirect_uri=…&state=…, where {shop} is the store's myshopify.com domain. Store the state to check it on the callback.

steps.text: Browser: open the authorize link for your development store and approve the app.
steps.detail: Shopify's callback carries code, hmac, shop, state and timestamp. Validate all of them before exchanging the code at https://{shop}/admin/oauth/access_token.

steps.text: Dev Dashboard → app Home → Distribution card: click Select distribution method, choose Public distribution and confirm.
steps.detail: The choice cannot be changed afterwards.

steps.text: Partner Dashboard → Apps → your app → API access requests: request protected customer data access if your scopes need it.
steps.detail: Request the fields you use individually.

steps.text: Shopify App Store review page: fix flagged issues, then click Submit your app.
Shopify App Store review page: wait for Shopify's reviewer; reply to emails if the app moves to Reviewed.
steps.detail: After approval the app moves to Published.

blockers.problem: Authorization fails with missing_shopify_permission for a scope.
blockers.fix: Request approval for that scope in the Partner Dashboard or via Shopify Support before declaring it.

blockers.problem: Customer fields come back null with 'This app is not approved to access the Customer object'.
blockers.fix: Select the fields in the Partner Dashboard; outside development stores, get protected customer data approval.
Pair read_all_orders with read_orders or write_orders and request approval.

blockers.problem: API calls start failing an hour after the store connects.
blockers.fix: Expiring offline tokens last 1 hour; refresh them with the refresh token, which lasts 90 days. New public apps can't use non-expiring tokens.

blockers.problem: Scopes added in a new version don't work on stores that already installed the app.
blockers.fix: Ask those merchants to approve the new scopes in the Shopify admin.

couldNotVerify: The amount of the App Store registration fee.

claims.statement: Apps installed only on development stores do not need a protected customer data review.
claims.quote: You don't need to submit a request for review for apps that are installed only on development stores.

claims.statement: The API won't return protected customer data from non-development stores until the app is approved.
claims.quote: You can add the relevant scopes to your app, but the API won't return data from non-development stores until your app is configured and approved for protected customer data use.

claims.statement: Submitted apps go through an app review process.
claims.quote: When you submit an app, it goes through an app review process to make sure that it meets Shopify's requirements for safe, quality apps .

claims.statement: The developer submits by clicking Submit your app after fixing issues.
claims.quote: When you create a public app, it starts with the Draft status. You must fix any issues that are identified on the Shopify App Store review page before you can submit your app for review. After you make the changes, you can click the Submit your app button to send your app for review.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Development stores are used to install and test apps.
claims.sourceTitle: Everything You Need to Know About Development Stores - Shopify
claims.quote: You can use them for testing and installing your apps, providing example stores running your app, and for signing up clients to Shopify.

claims.statement: The redirect URI must be added in the Dev Dashboard and match exactly; client ID and secret come from the Dev Dashboard.
claims.sourceTitle: Authenticate a standalone or API-only app
claims.quote: App credentials You have your app's client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard. … Redirect URI You've added your app's redirect URI to your app's settings in the Dev Dashboard, or to the [auth] section of your shopify.app.toml . … Must exactly match a redirect URI you've configured in the Dev Dashboard or your app's configuration TOML file.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: read_orders and write_orders cover the last 60 days; read_all_orders extends that.
claims.quote: By default, read_orders provides read access and write_orders provides read and write access to orders created within the last 60 days. read_all_orders doesn't grant access on its own. Declare it alongside read_orders or write_orders to extend that scope's access to older orders:
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: Write scopes include read access.
claims.quote: Any scope that writes a resource also grants read access to it, so request the write scope only when your app needs both.

claims.statement: Some scopes need Shopify approval before they can be requested.
claims.quote: The OAuth error reads missing_shopify_permission: <scope> , and the same failure on the GraphQL path reads Shopify needs to approve the following access scopes: <names> .

claims.statement: Selecting a distribution method is done from the app Home Distribution card.
claims.quote: On the app's Home , find the Distribution card and click Select distribution method .

claims.statement: The merchant is redirected to Shopify, approves, and the app exchanges a code for an access token.
claims.sourceTitle: Authenticate a standalone or API-only app
claims.quote: Because they can't use ID tokens , they authenticate using the OAuth authorization code grant flow: redirect the merchant to Shopify, get their approval, and exchange a code for an access token.

claims.statement: Protected customer data access is requested in the Partner Dashboard under API access requests.
claims.quote: From the Partner Dashboard, go to Apps , and then select your app. … In the sidebar, click API access requests . … Find Protected customer data access and click Request access .
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: After submission a reviewer is assigned and the app can move to Reviewed requiring a reply by email.
claims.quote: After your app meets the core requirements, Shopify assigns a reviewer to your submission, and they begin to review your app. If your app requires additional fixes that need to be discussed with your reviewer, then it moves to the Reviewed status. You'll receive an email that outlines the next steps and you need to reply to continue the process.
claims.note: [Re-quoted automatically: the first quote didn't state this.]

claims.statement: After the app review team approves the app, the app moves to Published status and appears on the Shopify App Store.
claims.quote: After your app has been approved by the app review team, you'll receive an email confirming that your app has moved to the Published status and now displays on the Shopify App Store.

claims.statement: Create an app from Apps → Create app → Start from Dev Dashboard, then name it and select Create.
claims.sourceTitle: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard
claims.quote: From the Dev Dashboard, be sure you're on Apps in the left-panel navigation and select Create app in the top, right corner of the screen. Select Start from Dev Dashboard . Name your app, then select Create .
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: On the Versions page you set the App URL (a default works for apps not embedded in the admin) and scopes, then select Release; an app needs a version before any store can install it.
claims.sourceTitle: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard
claims.quote: Your app must have at least one version before it can be installed on a store. From the Versions page of your app in the Dev Dashboard, fill in the fields your app needs: App URL : Where Shopify loads your app. If your app isn't embedded in the Shopify admin, you can use the default https://shopify.dev/apps/default-app-home . … Then select Release .
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: The Client ID and Client secret are under App settings in the Dev Dashboard.
claims.sourceTitle: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard
claims.quote: From your app in the Dev Dashboard, select App settings . Copy your Client ID and Client secret .
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: The authorize URL is https://{shop}/admin/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope, redirect_uri and a random state you store and check later.
claims.sourceTitle: Authenticate a standalone or API-only app
claims.quote: Construct the authorization URL and redirect the merchant to it. Include a randomly generated state value (nonce) and store it so you can verify it in the next step. … const authUrl = `https:// ${ shop } /admin/oauth/authorize?` + new URLSearchParams ( { client_id : CLIENT_ID , scope : SCOPES , redirect_uri : REDIRECT_URI , state : nonce , } )
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: Shopify's callback carries code, hmac, shop, state and timestamp, and all of them must be validated before the code is exchanged.
claims.sourceTitle: Authenticate a standalone or API-only app
claims.quote: After the merchant approves your app, Shopify redirects to your redirect_uri with an authorization code and several query parameters. Validate all of them before exchanging the code. 1 https://your-app.example.com/callback?code={authorization_code}&hmac={hmac}&shop={shop}&state={nonce}&timestamp={timestamp}
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: Public apps must use expiring offline tokens for the GraphQL Admin API: new public apps can't use non-expiring ones, and existing public apps can't after January 1, 2027.
claims.quote: Use expiring offline access tokens for public apps that call the GraphQL Admin API. … Non-expiring offline tokens grant permanent access until the app is uninstalled or the secret is revoked. New public apps already can't use them for GraphQL Admin API requests, and existing public apps can't after January 1, 2027.
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: An expiring offline access token lasts 1 hour; its refresh token lasts 90 days when issued.
claims.quote: Expiring offline access token 1 hour ( expires_in is 3600 ) Refresh token for an expiring offline access token 90 days ( refresh_token_expires_in is 7776000 ) when issued.
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: New scopes in a later version aren't applied to installed stores until merchants approve them in the Shopify admin.
claims.sourceTitle: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard
claims.quote: When you update scopes in a new version of your app, updates aren't applied automatically to the stores your app is installed on. Merchants still need to manually approve the new scopes in the Shopify admin.
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.

claims.statement: Creating apps requires app development permissions.
claims.sourceTitle: Create apps using the Dev Dashboard
claims.quote: Requirements You're a user with app development permissions .
claims.note: Checked by hand on 2026-10-29.
